recommendations.title: Professional Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Type 2 Diabetes Management
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement professional continuous glucose monitoring (P-CGM) for selected patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes; identify candidates with A1C above target despite standard therapy; coordinate device placement and removal; educate patients on wearing sensor without disrupting daily activities; download and analyze glucose pattern data; review results with patients highlighting glucose trends, hypoglycemic events, and postprandial patterns; use data to guide medication adjustments and lifestyle modifications; document findings and interventions.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved glycemic control, reduced hypoglycemic events, enhanced understanding of glucose patterns, better-informed medication adjustments, increased patient engagement, improved dietary choices based on glucose response data, more effective diabetes self-management.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes who have A1C above target despite standard therapy, those with suspected hypoglycemia, or patients with limited SMBG data.
recommendations.citation: Shrivastav M, Gibson W Jr, Shrivastav R, et al. Type 2 diabetes management in primary care: the role of retrospective, professional continuous glucose monitoring. Diabetes Spectr. 2018;31(3):279-287. doi:10.2337/ds17-0024

recommendations.title: Evidence-Based Diabetes Management for Primary Care Providers
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a comprehensive approach to diabetes management that includes: 1) Conduct regular screenings and assessments; 2) Develop individualized care plans; 3) Provide patient education using teach-back methods; 4) Coordinate care with specialists; 5) Monitor outcomes and adjust interventions as needed; 6) Address social determinants of health; 7) Utilize evidence-based protocols; 8) Engage family and caregivers in the care process; 9) Document interventions and outcomes; 10) Follow up regularly to ensure adherence and address barriers.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved diabetes management, reduced complications, enhanced quality of life, decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved patient satisfaction, better medication adherence, increased patient self-management skills, reduced healthcare disparities.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals, particularly those from underserved communities, racial and ethnic minorities, and those facing barriers to healthcare access.
recommendations.citation: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Evidence-Based Practice Guidelines for Diabetes Management in Primary Care Settings. https://www.ahrq.gov/research/findings/evidence-based-reports/search.html. Published 2023. Accessed May 29, 2025.

recommendations.title: Standardized Blood Pressure Measurement Protocol
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement standardized blood pressure measurement protocol; ensure patient is seated comfortably with back supported and feet flat on floor for 5 minutes before measurement; position arm at heart level with palm facing up; use appropriately sized cuff (bladder encircling 80% of arm); take at least 2 readings 1-2 minutes apart and average results; document which arm was used and position; avoid measuring after caffeine, exercise, or full bladder; train all staff on proper technique; consider implementing automated office blood pressure measurement when available.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved accuracy of blood pressure readings, reduced misdiagnosis of hypertension, better-informed treatment decisions, enhanced identification of white coat and masked hypertension, improved blood pressure control rates, reduced unnecessary medication adjustments.
recommendations.target_population: All Medicaid-enrolled adults requiring blood pressure assessment, particularly those with diagnosed or suspected hypertension.
recommendations.citation: Carey RM, Wright JT Jr, Taler SJ, Whelton PK. Guideline-driven management of hypertension: an evidence-based update. Circ Res. 2021;128(7):827-846. doi:10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.121.318083

recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved hypertension management, reduced complications, enhanced quality of life, decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved patient satisfaction, better medication adherence, increased patient self-management skills, reduced healthcare disparities.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals, particularly those from underserved communities, racial and ethnic minorities, and those facing barriers to healthcare access.
recommendations.citation: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Evidence-Based Practice Guidelines for Hypertension Management in Primary Care Settings. https://www.ahrq.gov/research/findings/evidence-based-reports/search.html. Published 2023. Accessed May 29, 2025.

recommendations.title: Universal Depression Screening Protocol with Measurement-Based Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement universal depression screening using PHQ-2 for all adult patients; follow positive screens (score ≥3) with PHQ-9 assessment; document scores in structured fields; establish workflow for same-day provider review of positive screens; develop protocol for measurement-based care including standardized follow-up intervals (4-6 weeks initially); use PHQ-9 at each follow-up to track symptom improvement; create registry to monitor patients with positive screens; establish clear referral pathways for severe cases or suicidal ideation; train all staff on screening workflow and documentation.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved identification of depression, enhanced treatment monitoring, better clinical outcomes, reduced symptom severity, increased remission rates, systematic follow-up of diagnosed patients, improved documentation of depression care, reduced missed opportunities for intervention.
recommendations.target_population: All Medicaid-enrolled adults in primary care settings, with particular attention to those with chronic medical conditions, recent life stressors, or previous history of depression.
recommendations.citation: Siniscalchi KA, Broome ME, Fish J, et al. Depression screening and measurement-based care in primary care. J Prim Care Community Health. 2020;11:2150132720931261. doi:10.1177/2150132720931261

recommendations.title: Stepped-Care Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Anxiety in Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a stepped-care approach to CBT for anxiety disorders; begin with low-intensity interventions for mild to moderate anxiety including guided self-help materials and computerized/internet-delivered CBT programs; provide brief psychoeducation about anxiety symptoms and cognitive-behavioral model; teach specific relaxation techniques including diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation; assign homework for skill practice; monitor symptoms using validated measures (GAD-7, PHQ-4); escalate to higher-intensity face-to-face CBT for non-responders or more severe cases; consider group-based CBT when appropriate; maintain regular communication with primary care provider about treatment progress.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced anxiety symptoms, improved functional status, decreased healthcare utilization, enhanced self-management skills, improved quality of life, reduced need for pharmacotherapy, increased treatment accessibility, cost-effective care delivery.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled adults with diagnosed anxiety disorders or elevated anxiety symptoms in primary care settings, particularly those with mild to moderate severity who may benefit from non-specialist interventions.
recommendations.citation: Parker EL, Banfield M, Fassnacht DB, Hatfield T, Kyrios M. Contemporary treatment of anxiety in primary care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of outcomes in countries with universal healthcare. BMC Fam Pract. 2021;22(1):92. doi:10.1186/s12875-021-01445-5

recommendations.title: Integrated Primary Care Model for Youth Substance Use Disorders
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement an integrated primary care model for adolescents and young adults with substance use disorders; establish a multidisciplinary team including primary care, addiction treatment, mental health, and social services; screen all youth for substance use using validated tools (CRAFFT, S2BI); provide same-day access when possible; offer medications for opioid use disorder when indicated; incorporate harm reduction strategies including naloxone distribution; address co-occurring mental health conditions through integrated behavioral health services; develop proactive re-engagement strategies for youth who miss appointments; create flexible scheduling options; establish clear protocols for managing polysubstance use; coordinate with community resources for housing and other social needs.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved identification of substance use disorders, increased engagement in treatment, enhanced retention in care, reduced substance-related harms, better management of co-occurring mental health conditions, improved coordination of care, increased access to evidence-based treatments, reduced barriers to care.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled adolescents and young adults (ages 14-26) with substance use disorders or problematic substance use, particularly those with co-occurring mental health conditions or housing instability.
recommendations.citation: Bagley SM, Hadland SE, Schoenberger SF, et al. Integrating substance use care into primary care for adolescents and young adults: Lessons learned. J Subst Abuse Treat. 2021;129:108376. doi:10.1016/j.jsat.2021.108376

recommendations.citation: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Evidence-Based Practice Guidelines for Substance Use Management in Primary Care Settings. https://www.ahrq.gov/research/findings/evidence-based-reports/search.html. Published 2023. Accessed May 29, 2025.

recommendations.title: Housing Stability Intervention for Health Improvement
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a housing stability assessment and intervention protocol; screen all Medicaid patients for housing instability using validated questions about housing security, eviction risk, and homelessness; document housing status in structured fields; create referral pathways to local housing assistance programs; develop relationships with legal aid services for eviction prevention; coordinate with rental assistance programs; maintain updated resource list of emergency housing options; assist patients with housing applications and documentation requirements; follow up within 30 days to assess housing status changes; provide transportation assistance to housing appointments when needed; advocate with landlords when appropriate; document all housing interventions and outcomes.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced housing instability, decreased emergency department utilization, improved chronic disease management, better medication adherence, reduced missed appointments, improved mental health outcomes, decreased hospitalization rates, cost savings to Medicaid system.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals experiencing or at risk of housing instability, particularly those with chronic health conditions, behavioral health diagnoses, or high healthcare utilization patterns.
recommendations.citation: Taylor LA. Housing and health: an overview of the literature. Health Affairs Health Policy Brief. 2018. doi:10.1377/hpb20180313.396577

recommendations.title: Standardized Food Insecurity Screening and Referral Protocol
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a standardized two-question food insecurity screening tool (Hunger Vital Sign) during all routine primary care visits; integrate screening questions into electronic health record templates; document food insecurity status in structured fields; establish clear workflow for positive screens including same-day referrals to food assistance programs; develop partnerships with local food banks and SNAP outreach programs; create resource guide of local food assistance options; provide patients with direct referrals rather than passive information; follow up on referrals within two weeks; track referral outcomes; consider implementing food pharmacy or medically-tailored meal programs for patients with diet-related chronic conditions; rescreen at 6-month intervals or with significant life changes.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Increased identification of food insecurity, improved connection to food assistance resources, better management of diet-related chronic conditions, reduced emergency department utilization, improved medication adherence, enhanced patient trust and engagement, reduced healthcare costs.
recommendations.target_population: All Medicaid-enrolled patients, with particular focus on households with children, older adults, those with chronic health conditions, and individuals living in low-income neighborhoods.
recommendations.citation: Odoms-Young A, Brown AGM, Agurs-Collins T, Glanz K. Food insecurity, neighborhood food environment, and health disparities: state of the science, research gaps and opportunities. Am J Clin Nutr. 2023;119(3):850-861. doi:10.1016/j.ajcnut.2023.12.019

recommendations.title: Transportation Voucher Program for Chronic Disease Management
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a transportation voucher program for patients with chronic diseases; assess transportation needs during intake and follow-up appointments; document transportation barriers in structured EHR fields; provide bus passes, taxi vouchers, or rideshare credits based on patient needs and preferences; establish partnerships with local transportation providers; create clear eligibility criteria focusing on patients with multiple chronic conditions or frequent missed appointments; develop a simple request process requiring minimal paperwork; track utilization patterns and appointment adherence; follow up with patients who continue to miss appointments despite transportation assistance; coordinate with social workers for patients with complex needs; consider implementing a volunteer driver program for rural areas; evaluate program effectiveness by monitoring appointment attendance rates.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced missed appointments, improved chronic disease management, decreased emergency department utilization, enhanced medication adherence, better continuity of care, increased patient satisfaction, reduced healthcare costs, improved health outcomes.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals with chronic diseases who face transportation barriers to healthcare access, particularly those in rural areas, without access to vehicles, with mobility limitations, or with multiple chronic conditions requiring frequent appointments.

recommendations.title: Home-Based Asthma Management Program for Medicaid Children
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a structured home-based asthma management program; conduct comprehensive home environmental assessments using standardized tools; identify and address asthma triggers including dust mites, mold, pests, and tobacco smoke; provide allergen-proof mattress and pillow covers; demonstrate proper inhaler technique and medication use; develop personalized asthma action plans in partnership with primary care providers; educate families on early symptom recognition; schedule follow-up home visits at 1, 3, and 6 months; coordinate with school nurses to ensure consistent asthma management; track symptom frequency, emergency department visits, and hospitalizations; connect families with resources for remediation of environmental triggers; provide culturally appropriate education materials in preferred language.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced asthma-related emergency department visits, decreased hospitalizations, improved medication adherence, reduced school absences, enhanced quality of life, improved asthma control test scores, decreased exposure to environmental triggers, reduced healthcare costs.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled children with poorly controlled asthma, particularly those with recent emergency department visits or hospitalizations, living in urban environments with high asthma prevalence.
recommendations.citation: Center for Health Care Strategies. Improving Asthma Care for Children: Best Practices in Medicaid Managed Care. CHCS Toolkit. 2018.

recommendations.title: Standardized COPD Screening and Management Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement systematic screening for COPD in all smokers and ex-smokers over 40 years old using office spirometry; integrate spirometry into routine care with clear workflow; document smoking history and occupational exposures; assess severity using both FEV1 and validated tools like the BODE index (Body mass index, airflow Obstruction, Dyspnea, Exercise capacity); evaluate for systemic manifestations including cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, muscle dysfunction, depression, and anxiety; provide smoking cessation counseling and pharmacotherapy; prescribe appropriate inhaler therapy based on symptom severity and exacerbation history; ensure proper inhaler technique through demonstration and teach-back; refer to pulmonary rehabilitation for moderate to severe disease; screen for and address comorbidities; develop action plans for exacerbations; schedule regular follow-up visits at 3-6 month intervals.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved early detection of COPD, reduced exacerbations, decreased hospitalizations, enhanced quality of life, improved exercise capacity, better medication adherence, reduced emergency department visits, slowed disease progression through smoking cessation.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients who are current or former smokers over 40 years old, particularly those with respiratory symptoms, frequent respiratory infections, or occupational exposures.

recommendations.title: Comprehensive Heart Failure Management Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a structured approach to heart failure management in primary care; use natriuretic peptide testing (NT-proBNP) with a threshold of 125 pg/ml to screen patients with suspected heart failure; refer patients with positive results or history of myocardial infarction for echocardiography; classify heart failure based on ejection fraction (HFrEF <40%, HFmrEF 40-49%, HFpEF ≥50%); prescribe diuretics for symptom relief in all types; for HFrEF, initiate and titrate ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists to target doses; consider ARNI therapy (sacubitril/valsartan) for patients who remain symptomatic despite optimal therapy; assess for comorbidities including renal dysfunction, anemia, and atrial fibrillation; provide patient education on self-care, including daily weight monitoring, salt restriction, and fluid management; develop personalized care plans addressing lifestyle modifications; schedule regular follow-up visits at 1-3 month intervals during medication titration.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced heart failure hospitalizations, decreased mortality, improved quality of life, enhanced functional capacity, better medication adherence, reduced symptom burden, improved patient self-management, decreased healthcare costs.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients with suspected or confirmed heart failure, particularly those with cardiovascular risk factors, history of myocardial infarction, or symptoms of dyspnea, fatigue, and fluid retention.
recommendations.citation: Taylor CJ, Rutten FH, Brouwer JR, Hobbs FDR. Practical guidance on heart failure diagnosis and management in primary care: recent EPCCS recommendations. Br J Gen Pract. 2017;67(660):326-327. doi:10.3399/bjgp17X691553

recommendations.title: Comprehensive Preventive Screening Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a systematic approach to preventive screenings based on USPSTF A and B recommendations; screen for anxiety disorders in adults under 65, including pregnant and postpartum persons; screen for anxiety in children and adolescents aged 8-18 years; screen for depression in adults, including pregnant and postpartum persons; screen for major depressive disorder in adolescents aged 12-18; provide low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) after 12 weeks gestation for pregnant persons at high risk for preeclampsia; screen for asymptomatic bacteriuria using urine culture in pregnant persons; assess women with personal or family history of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer for BRCA testing; offer risk-reducing medications for breast cancer to high-risk women; conduct biennial mammography screening for women aged 40-74; screen for cervical cancer every 3 years with cytology alone for women 21-29, and every 3-5 years with cytology or HPV testing for women 30-65; screen for chlamydia and gonorrhea in sexually active women 24 or younger and older women at increased risk; screen for colorectal cancer in adults aged 45-75 using appropriate modalities.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Increased early detection of diseases, reduced morbidity and mortality, improved quality of life, decreased healthcare costs through prevention, enhanced patient engagement in preventive care, reduced disparities in preventive service utilization.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals across the lifespan, with particular attention to those with limited access to preventive services, racial and ethnic minorities, and those with social determinants of health barriers.

recommendations.title: Structured Medication Adherence Intervention for Chronic Disease Management
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a comprehensive medication adherence program for patients with chronic diseases; conduct standardized medication adherence assessments using validated tools (e.g., Morisky Medication Adherence Scale) at each visit; document adherence status in structured EHR fields; identify specific barriers to adherence through targeted questioning; provide tailored patient education on medication purpose, dosage, timing, and potential side effects; use teach-back method to confirm understanding; simplify medication regimens when possible through collaboration with prescribers; implement pill organizers or blister packs for patients with complex regimens; establish medication reminder systems (e.g., phone apps, text messages); engage family members or caregivers in medication management; schedule regular follow-up calls between visits to address adherence challenges; coordinate with pharmacists for medication reviews; document and address adverse effects promptly; create personalized medication schedules aligned with patient's daily routines.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates, better chronic disease control, reduced hospital admissions, decreased emergency department visits, enhanced quality of life, improved clinical outcomes, reduced healthcare costs, increased patient knowledge and self-efficacy.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients with chronic diseases requiring long-term medication therapy, particularly those with multiple medications, complex regimens, or history of poor adherence.
recommendations.citation: Oliveira CJ, José HMG, Costa EIMT. Medication Adherence in Adults with Chronic Diseases in Primary Healthcare: A Quality Improvement Project. Nurs Rep. 2024;14(3):1735-1749. doi:10.3390/nursrep14030129

recommendations.title: Care Transitions Intervention (CTI) for Hospital-to-Home Transitions
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement the evidence-based Care Transitions Intervention (CTI) model for patients transitioning from hospital to home; assign a trained Transitions Coach to work with patients for a 30-day period; conduct one home visit within 24-72 hours of discharge and three follow-up phone calls; focus on four key pillars: medication self-management, use of a dynamic patient-centered health record, primary care/specialist follow-up, and knowledge of red flags; teach patients to use a personal health record to track medications, questions for providers, and follow-up appointments; coach patients to schedule and prepare for follow-up appointments rather than doing it for them; help patients identify and respond to red flags that indicate worsening condition; conduct medication reconciliation during the home visit; use role-playing to practice communication with healthcare providers; emphasize skill transfer and patient empowerment rather than performing tasks for patients; document patient activation scores at baseline and program completion.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced hospital readmission rates, improved patient activation and self-management skills, successful patient-identified goal achievement, decreased emergency department visits, improved medication management, enhanced communication with healthcare providers, reduced healthcare costs.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients with complex care needs transitioning from hospital to home, particularly those with chronic conditions, complex medication regimens, or at high risk for readmission.
recommendations.citation: National Council on Aging. Evidence-Based Program: Care Transitions Intervention. https://www.ncoa.org/article/evidence-based-program-care-transitions-intervention. Published November 1, 2023. Accessed May 29, 2025.

recommendations.title: Comprehensive CKD Management Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a systematic approach to CKD management in primary care; screen high-risk patients (diabetes, hypertension, family history of kidney disease) with both eGFR and urinary albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR); consider cystatin C testing for further risk stratification in patients with eGFR 45-59 ml/min/1.73m² without albuminuria; document CKD diagnosis in problem list when confirmed with two abnormal eGFR values at least 90 days apart; optimize blood pressure control with target <130/80 mmHg for those with albuminuria; prescribe ACE inhibitors or ARBs for patients with albuminuria; initiate SGLT2 inhibitors for patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuria; prescribe statins for cardiovascular risk reduction in patients over 50; monitor potassium levels in patients on RAAS inhibitors; educate patients about their CKD diagnosis, importance of medication adherence, and self-management strategies; refer to nephrology for eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73m², rapid decline in kidney function, or persistent albuminuria despite optimal therapy.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Improved CKD awareness among providers and patients, earlier detection of CKD, slowed progression of kidney disease, reduced cardiovascular events, decreased progression to kidney failure, improved medication adherence, enhanced patient self-management, reduced hospitalizations.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients with CKD or at high risk for CKD, particularly those with diabetes, hypertension, or family history of kidney disease.
recommendations.citation: Foti K, Chang AR. Chronic Kidney Disease Management in Primary Care: Supporting Systems Change. Am J Kidney Dis. 2020;76(5):613-615. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.07.008

recommendations.title: Comprehensive Post-MI Management Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a structured approach to post-MI care during the subacute period (1-3 months post-discharge); review discharge medications and ensure patient is on guideline-directed medical therapy including: daily aspirin 75-162mg, P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel, prasugrel, or ticagrelor) for up to 12 months, beta-blocker therapy (especially for patients with LVEF ≤40%), ACE inhibitor or ARB (particularly for patients with LVEF ≤40%, hypertension, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease), and high-intensity statin therapy; schedule follow-up appointment within 1-2 weeks of discharge; perform medication reconciliation at each visit; assess medication adherence and address barriers; refer to cardiac rehabilitation within 1-2 weeks of discharge; provide clear activity recommendations with gradual return to normal activities; educate patient on lifestyle modifications including smoking cessation, heart-healthy diet, weight management, and regular physical activity; teach recognition of cardiac symptoms requiring medical attention; arrange early non-invasive stress testing for risk stratification in patients who did not undergo revascularization; implement structured communication with cardiologists for coordinated care; monitor for depression and provide appropriate treatment or referral.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced hospital readmissions, decreased recurrent MI risk, improved medication adherence, increased cardiac rehabilitation participation, enhanced quality of life, reduced all-cause mortality, improved functional capacity, better patient self-management, decreased healthcare costs.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients in the subacute period following myocardial infarction.
recommendations.citation: Mercado MG, Smith DK, McConnon ML. Myocardial infarction: management of the subacute period. Am Fam Physician. 2013;88(9):581-588.

recommendations.title: Comprehensive Post-Stroke Management Protocol for Primary Care
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a structured approach to post-stroke care; schedule first follow-up visit within 1-3 weeks of hospital discharge; establish a foundation for care by understanding the patient's experience and concerns; review stroke etiology and ensure diagnostic workup is complete (including carotid imaging and prolonged cardiac monitoring when indicated); review discharge medications and ensure patient is on appropriate secondary prevention therapy including antithrombotic therapy, antihypertensives, and statins; screen for post-stroke complications including depression (using PHQ-9), cognitive impairment (using Montreal Cognitive Assessment), and fall risk; assess for unmet rehabilitation needs in mobility, activities of daily living, and communication; manage vascular risk factors with target blood pressure <130/80 mmHg for most patients; ensure appropriate anticoagulation for patients with atrial fibrillation; optimize diabetes management with target HbA1c <7%; refer to appropriate rehabilitation services for ongoing functional impairments; provide education on lifestyle modifications including Mediterranean or DASH diet, regular physical activity, smoking cessation, and limited alcohol consumption; engage caregivers and family members in the care plan; establish a clear follow-up schedule with regular reassessment of needs.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced risk of recurrent stroke, improved functional status, decreased post-stroke complications, enhanced quality of life, reduced hospital readmissions, improved medication adherence, better risk factor control, increased patient and caregiver engagement, reduced caregiver burden.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled patients following stroke discharge, particularly those with ongoing functional impairments or multiple vascular risk factors.
recommendations.citation: Kernan WN, Viera AJ, Billinger SA, et al. Primary Care of Adult Patients After Stroke: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Stroke. 2021;52(9):e558-e571. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000382

recommendations.title: Comprehensive HIV Primary Care for Medicaid-Enrolled Patients
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a comprehensive HIV primary care approach that includes: 1) Create a stigma-free, culturally appropriate care environment to maximize engagement; 2) Screen for and address barriers to care at societal, health system, clinic, and individual levels; 3) Ensure continuous access to antiretroviral therapy (ART) with regular adherence assessment and support; 4) Monitor HIV viral load every 3-4 months once suppressed, and CD4 count at least annually; 5) Screen for and manage common comorbidities including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, renal disease, bone health issues, and mental health conditions; 6) Provide age-appropriate cancer screenings with particular attention to HPV-related cancers; 7) Conduct regular STI screening (at least annually, more frequently based on risk) including syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia, and hepatitis; 8) Ensure complete vaccination series including pneumococcal (PCV13 and PPV23), hepatitis A and B, influenza, and COVID-19; 9) Implement substance use screening and harm reduction strategies; 10) Address reproductive health needs including contraception and preconception counseling; 11) Provide tailored care for special populations including adolescents and transgender individuals; 12) Utilize multidisciplinary teams and telehealth when appropriate to improve access; 13) Implement systems to identify and re-engage patients who miss appointments.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Sustained HIV viral suppression, reduced HIV-related morbidity and mortality, prevention of HIV transmission, improved management of comorbidities, increased vaccination rates, reduced STI rates, improved quality of life, decreased healthcare disparities, reduced emergency department utilization, and improved long-term retention in care.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals living with HIV, particularly those from underserved communities, racial and ethnic minorities, and those facing barriers to consistent healthcare access.
recommendations.citation: Horberg M, Thompson M, Agwu A, et al. Primary Care Guidance for Providers Who Care for Persons With Human Immunodeficiency Virus: 2024 Update by HIVMA/IDSA. Clin Infect Dis. 2024;ciae479. doi:10.1093/cid/ciae479

recommendations.title: Evidence-Based Vaccination Implementation Strategy for Medicaid Populations
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a comprehensive vaccination strategy for Medicaid-enrolled patients that includes: 1) Assess vaccination status at every clinical encounter using electronic health records or immunization information systems; 2) Strongly recommend needed vaccines using presumptive language (e.g., 'Today you are due for these vaccines' rather than 'Would you like vaccines today?'); 3) Address vaccine hesitancy with motivational interviewing techniques and culturally appropriate education materials; 4) Implement standing orders to allow nursing staff to administer vaccines without physician examination; 5) Use reminder/recall systems (text messages, phone calls, letters) to notify patients of due or overdue vaccines; 6) Schedule dedicated vaccination-only appointments when needed; 7) Offer extended hours or weekend vaccination clinics to accommodate working patients; 8) Implement simultaneous administration of multiple needed vaccines when appropriate; 9) Document vaccine refusals and reasons in the medical record for follow-up at subsequent visits; 10) Provide vaccine information statements in the patient's preferred language; 11) Utilize every opportunity to vaccinate including sick visits when appropriate; 12) Report all administered vaccines to state/regional immunization information systems; 13) Implement quality improvement processes to track and improve vaccination rates; 14) Address transportation barriers through mobile vaccination services or transportation assistance when possible.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Increased vaccination rates, reduced vaccine-preventable diseases, decreased healthcare disparities in immunization coverage, reduced emergency department visits and hospitalizations for vaccine-preventable conditions, improved herd immunity in vulnerable communities, increased patient satisfaction with preventive care, reduced costs associated with vaccine-preventable diseases.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals across the lifespan, with particular focus on children, pregnant individuals, adults with chronic conditions, and older adults who may face barriers to vaccination.
recommendations.citation: Kroger A, Bahta L, Long S, Sanchez P. General Best Practice Guidelines for Immunization. Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/acip-recs/general-recs/downloads/general-recs.pdf. Accessed May 29, 2025.

recommendations.title: Community-Based Doula Support for Prenatal Care in Underserved Populations
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a community-based doula program for Medicaid-enrolled pregnant individuals; recruit and train doulas from the local community who reflect the racial and cultural diversity of the population served; establish a referral system with local obstetric providers to identify pregnant individuals who would benefit from doula support; initiate doula services early in pregnancy (ideally first trimester); provide continuous psychosocial, emotional, and educational support throughout pregnancy; conduct regular home visits to build trust and address social determinants of health; assist with birth planning and preparation; advocate for patient preferences during medical appointments; provide coaching on communicating effectively with healthcare providers; educate on pregnancy warning signs and when to seek medical care; connect patients to community resources for food security, housing, and transportation; accompany patients to prenatal appointments when needed; help navigate insurance and healthcare systems; document services provided and outcomes for program evaluation; coordinate with the healthcare team to ensure integrated care; provide culturally appropriate education on nutrition, physical activity, and self-care during pregnancy.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Reduced birth complications, decreased rates of low birthweight babies, increased attendance at prenatal appointments, improved patient satisfaction with care, reduced racial disparities in birth outcomes, increased breastfeeding initiation, decreased preterm births, enhanced patient self-advocacy, improved maternal mental health, stronger connection to healthcare system.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant individuals, particularly those from racial and ethnic minority groups, those with low income, and those facing barriers to accessing quality prenatal care.

recommendations.title: Comprehensive Postpartum Care Strategy for Medicaid Populations
recommendations.implementation_guidance: Implement a multi-component postpartum care strategy that includes: 1) Schedule the first postpartum visit within 1-2 weeks after delivery, rather than waiting for the traditional 6-week visit; 2) Use reminder systems including text messages, phone calls, and mail notifications to improve attendance; 3) Conduct comprehensive screenings at postpartum visits including depression (using PHQ-9), anxiety, substance use, intimate partner violence, and social determinants of health; 4) Provide contraceptive counseling and same-day access to contraceptive methods of choice; 5) Assess breastfeeding status and provide lactation support or referrals as needed; 6) Screen for chronic conditions that may have developed during pregnancy (hypertension, diabetes) and establish appropriate follow-up care; 7) Coordinate care with pediatric providers to align maternal postpartum visits with infant well-visits; 8) Implement flexible scheduling options including evening and weekend appointments; 9) Offer telehealth options when appropriate for follow-up care; 10) Address transportation barriers through ride-sharing services or transportation vouchers; 11) Provide culturally and linguistically appropriate education materials on postpartum warning signs and when to seek care; 12) Establish a system to track patients who miss appointments and conduct outreach.
recommendations.expected_outcomes: Increased postpartum visit attendance rates, improved identification and management of postpartum complications, reduced emergency department utilization, increased contraceptive uptake, improved breastfeeding continuation rates, better management of chronic conditions, reduced postpartum depression, improved patient satisfaction with care, reduced racial disparities in postpartum care utilization.
recommendations.target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals in the postpartum period, particularly those from racial and ethnic minority groups and those facing barriers to accessing care.
